Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 4913 of 2023
Applicant :- Arvind
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Civil Secrett. Lko.

And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjay Kumar Yadav,Pramod Kumar,Pratiti,Siddharth Soni

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard Ms. Pratiti, learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
No one appears on behalf of the complainant despite service of notice.

2. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant aged about 16 years informed her Aunt that about four months ago, one Raj Kumar threatened her by showing a knife and committed wrong on her and she was carrying a fetus of said Raj Kumar.
Subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim once again reiterated the prosecution story and made allegation against Raj Kumar.
Thereafter on examination before the medical officer, the victim once again referred the name of Raj Kumar.
The medical was conducted on 02.08.2022, which Arvind vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

1 demonstrated that the victim was carrying a fetus of 26 weeks.

3 . The counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.,
wherein the victim stated that around two years ago, the applicant came to the house of the victim and committed wrong on her on various occasion.
In the light of the said allegation, the applicant was linked and arrested for the offence in question.

It is further argued that the applicant was never named in the FIR or the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. or the statement given before the medical authority and as regards the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C, the same pertains to two years ago, whereas in the medical conducted on 01.08.2022, the victim was carrying a fetus of 26 weeks, thus according to the applicant there is no material whatsoever to link the applicant with the offence in question.
4.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer by arguing that not only was the applicant named in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., he has given a confessional statement which is filed as C.A.-8 to the counter affidavit, where he had admitted that the fetus was his and both of them wanted to marry.
There is no definite document with regard to the age of the victim as prescribed in the Juvenile Justice Act.

5. Considering the huge inconsistencies in the FIR, statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., statement before the medical authorities and the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. coupled with the fact the medical on record is not corroborated by the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., also coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 23.11.2022 and there no and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Arvind be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 487 of 2022, under Sections 376, 506 IPC and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Ramnagar, District Barabanki, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 15.4.2024 Arun  Arvind vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95125459/
